clue.text: Southern sailor has angles on marine creatures

parts.note: tar is an old word for a seaman
to angle is to fish with rod and line, so angles means fishes

explanation.surface: A sailor from the south has views about sea life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'angles' looks like a noun (viewpoints) but is the verb: an angler fishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Starfish are star-shaped invertebrates of the seabed, so they are sea animals.

clue.text: Whipping up loud fuss about reserve is enough

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters go round the loud and reserve pieces
whipping up stirs these letters into a fresh order

parts.note: F is forte, the musical direction for loud
ice means coolness or reserve of manner

explanation.surface: Stirring up a noisy commotion about restraint will do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whipping up' rearranges FUSS to SUFS, which goes about F and ICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Suffices means is adequate or meets the need.

clue.text: Off course in a heap of snow

parts.note: a drift is a bank of wind-blown snow

explanation.surface: Lost in a snowbank.
explanation.definitionFit: Adrift means drifting without control, so off one's intended route.

clue.text: Warning with spotlight peripherally lighting up group

parts.note: fore is the golfer's shouted warning

indicators.note: peripherally picks only the edge letters of spotlight

explanation.surface: An alert as a beam lights up a band of people.
explanation.definitionFit: A forest is a dense mass of trees, and by extension any thick cluster of upright things.

clue.text: Very low speaker to make an advance to solicitor holding bit of freehold

parts.note: to sub is to advance someone money from wages

indicators.note: holding means the suitor's letters enclose the next piece

parts.note: a solicitor here is one who solicits, a suitor or wooer

indicators.note: bit of takes just the first letter of freehold

explanation.surface: Lending money to a lawyer handling part of a property deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solicitor' suggests a British lawyer but is someone who woos.
explanation.definitionFit: A subwoofer is a loudspeaker reproducing only the deepest bass frequencies.

clue.text: No penalty as Celtic player's unimpeded

parts.note: a Celtic player is taken as a Scot, Celtic being a Glasgow football club
free means unhindered

explanation.surface: A Celtic footballer goes unchecked, so no penalty is given.
explanation.walkthrough: Celtic is a Glasgow football club; here its player is just a Scot.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting off scot-free means escaping punishment entirely.

clue.text: Little news of priestess embracing right-wing party

indicators.note: embracing means one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: Io was a priestess of Hera in Greek myth
NF is the National Front, a British far-right party

explanation.surface: Scant reporting about a priestess who joined an extremist party.
explanation.definitionFit: Info is a clipped, shortened form of information, so a small word for news or facts.

clue.text: Swarmed over jester in India once

indicators.note: in places the jester within the old name

parts.note: Ind was a poetic or old abbreviation for India
Feste is the jester in Shakespeare's Twelfth Night

explanation.surface: A clown in old India was mobbed.
explanation.definitionFit: Infested means overrun by pests in large numbers.

clue.text: Trick boyfriend with torch

parts.note: flam is an old word for a deception or trick
a beau is a boyfriend

explanation.surface: Fool a boyfriend with a flashlight.
explanation.definitionFit: A flambeau is a flaming torch, especially one carried in processions.

clue.text: Joints for eastern wives

parts.note: taken as written
Eve was made from Adam's rib, so a wife is jocularly a rib

explanation.surface: Cuts of meat suitable for women of the East.
explanation.walkthrough: Calling a wife a 'rib' recalls Genesis, where Eve is made from Adam's rib.
explanation.definitionFit: Fore ribs are a cut of beef roasted whole, so a meat joint in the butcher's sense.

clue.text: Exactly memorised start time covering each year

indicators.note: covering means the outer pieces sit around another piece

parts.note: the off is the start of a race
PA is per annum, Latin for each year

explanation.surface: A start time learned precisely, covering every year.
explanation.definitionFit: To have something off pat is to know it thoroughly by heart, word for word.

clue.text: Solution in coalition

parts.note: taken as written
a fusion is a joining together of parties or groups

explanation.surface: A political fix found by forming a coalition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solution' suggests an answer to a problem, but here it is a liquid with something steeped in it.
explanation.definitionFit: An infusion is liquid made by steeping herbs or tea, a kind of chemical solution.

clue.text: Close to promiscuous, heartless boy

parts.note: fast, of a person, means loose or sexually free

indicators.note: heartless says the middle letter of the word boy goes

parts.note: a boy is a young lad

explanation.surface: Near a loose-living, unfeeling young man.
explanation.definitionFit: Fast by is an archaic phrase meaning nearby, hard against, as in fast by the gate.

clue.text: Pipe sounding 'Gone Away'

indicators.note: sounding means we take how the word is pronounced, not spelt

parts.note: gone away in flight, as a bird does, is flew

explanation.surface: A hunting horn's call: 'Gone Away' is what huntsmen sound when the fox breaks cover.
explanation.definitionFit: A flue is a duct carrying smoke or air, essentially a pipe in a chimney or organ.

clue.text: Mad naif dunce not likely to succeed

indicators.note: mad suggests these letters are wildly disordered

explanation.surface: A crazy, innocent dimwit has little chance.
explanation.definitionFit: An unfancied runner is an outsider that few back to win.

clue.text: Loose alien priest in diocese

indicators.note: in places these two pieces inside the bishop's seat

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese
ET is the film alien, the Extra-Terrestrial
Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest

explanation.surface: A wayward foreign cleric at large in a bishop's territory.
explanation.definitionFit: To loose a captive is to release them, so it is a verb synonym of liberate.

clue.text: Enfield's got a broken rake

indicators.note: broken means the letters are smashed and reassembled

parts.note: the place name taken as written, its possessive adding no letter

explanation.surface: An Enfield rifle owner has a garden tool that's broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges ENFIELD and A; the Enfield is a British service rifle, which hints at the military sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To enfilade is to sweep a line of troops with gunfire along its length, to rake it.

clue.text: Smelly plant flourished by water near outskirts of Bayonne

parts.note: fl is floruit, flourished, in dates of a person's activity
ea is a dialect word for a river or stream

indicators.note: outskirts of keeps the outer parts of the town name and drops its centre

explanation.surface: A pungent plant that thrived near water on the edge of a French town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outskirts of' keeps BA and NE, losing the middle YON.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleabane is a plant once burnt to drive off fleas, valued for its strong odour.

clue.text: Blitzed figs gel softly for drinks

indicators.note: blitzed as in whizzed in a blender, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for softly

explanation.surface: Blended figs set gently into beverages.
explanation.definitionFit: Egg-flips are hot beverages of beaten egg with milk, beer or spirits.

clue.text: Nude elf — dressing up is required!

indicators.note: dressing up these letters puts them into a new disguise, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A naked elf: putting some clothes on is necessary!
explanation.definitionFit: Needful means necessary, a slightly old-fashioned word for what must be had or done.

clue.text: Officer holding unusual belief as aid to survival

indicators.note: holding means the officer's letters enclose the next piece

parts.note: Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant

indicators.note: unusual says the word belief is rearranged into an odd order

explanation.surface: An officer with a strange creed hopes it will save him.
explanation.definitionFit: A lifebelt is a buoyant ring thrown to keep someone afloat in water.

clue.text: Good fliers count in Germany

parts.note: the RAF, Royal Air Force, is Britain's body of airmen

explanation.surface: Skilled airmen are counted in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'count' looks like a verb but is the nobleman.
explanation.definitionFit: Graf is the German title equivalent to an earl or count.

clue.text: Barber's fair go for styling

indicators.note: styling, as a hairdresser does, reshapes these letters

explanation.surface: A hairdresser offers a decent chance at a new hairdo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for styling' rearranges FAIR GO; 'fair go' is an Australian phrase for a fair chance.
explanation.definitionFit: Figaro is the barber of Seville in the plays and operas of Beaumarchais, Rossini and Mozart.

clue.text: For offspring fill in first-class return? On the contrary

indicators.note: in would put fill inside the next piece
on the contrary flips that, so the turned pair goes inside fill

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: return means the first-class pair is turned round

parts.note: A1 means first class, its digit written as letter I

explanation.surface: For children, fill in the first-class return form.
explanation.definitionFit: Filial means relating to a son or daughter, so pertaining to offspring.

clue.text: Edith has left to join originator of fish dish

indicators.note: has means Piaf holds the next piece within her name

parts.note: Edith Piaf was the French singer

indicators.note: originator of picks the first letter of fish

explanation.surface: Edith departs to team up with the inventor of a seafood recipe.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilaff is a rice dish cooked in stock with spices, from the Middle East.

clue.text: In part of fish I note space

parts.note: taken as written
a fin is a fish's limb
taken as written
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Inside a bit of fish I spot a gap.
explanation.definitionFit: The infinite is boundless space or extent, the noun use of the adjective limitless.

clue.text: Expedition's at a distance in South Island

indicators.note: in says the far-off piece sits between the two abbreviations

parts.note: afar means far off, at a distance

explanation.surface: An expedition is far away, on New Zealand's South Island.
explanation.definitionFit: A safari is an organised expedition to observe or hunt wild animals.

clue.text: End stormy sail in beautiful surroundings

indicators.note: surroundings means the beautiful word goes round the jumbled letters

parts.note: fine can mean beautiful or handsome

indicators.note: stormy says the letters of sail are tossed about

explanation.surface: Ending a rough sea voyage in lovely scenery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End' looks like a noun but is the verb, to bring to a close.
explanation.definitionFit: To finalise is to complete or conclude, bring a matter to its end.

clue.text: Fine summer in France for holiday

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils
ete is French for summer

explanation.surface: A lovely French summer, ideal for a vacation.
explanation.definitionFit: A fete is a festival or feast day, a holiday of celebration.

clue.text: Accommodation for boss, one mostly recently

parts.note: a boss is a stud, a raised ornamental knob
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: mostly says the phrase loses its final letter

parts.note: of late means recently

explanation.surface: Housing for the boss, a single person, lately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boss' suggests an employer but is the round knob on a shield.
explanation.definitionFit: A studio flat is a one-room apartment, a common form of living space.
